gloss: to be absorbed in; to be immersed in

definitions.gloss: to be absorbed in; to be immersed in; to devote oneself to
definitions.explanation: To concentrate so deeply on an activity that one loses awareness of everything else. Often used for work, study, hobbies, or creative pursuits. Takes the particle に for the activity.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{研究|けんきゅう}に{没頭|ぼっとう}して{食事|しょくじ}も{忘|わす}れていた。
examples.english: She was so immersed in her research that she forgot to eat.

examples.japanese: {退職|たいしょく}してからは{趣味|しゅみ}の{絵画|かいが}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する{毎日|まいにち}を{送|おく}っている。
examples.english: Since retiring, I've been spending my days immersed in my hobby of painting.

notes:
PATTERN:
～に{没頭|ぼっとう}する (to be absorbed in ~)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する (to be absorbed in work)
- {研究|けんきゅう}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する (to be immersed in research)
- {勉強|べんきょう}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する (to be absorbed in studying)
- {読書|どくしょ}に{没頭|ぼっとう}する (to be absorbed in reading)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {夢中|むちゅう}になる: To be crazy about, absorbed in — more emotional and colloquial. Can be used for entertainment and fun activities more naturally.
- {集中|しゅうちゅう}する: To concentrate — more deliberate and controlled. {没頭|ぼっとう} implies losing oneself, while {集中|しゅうちゅう} implies focused effort.
- {熱中|ねっちゅう}する: To be enthusiastic about — emphasizes passion and excitement rather than deep focus.
